simple: F5’s cloud service for protecting websites and APIs (WAF for Distributed Cloud): it runs from F5’s global points of presence in front of applications in any cloud or your own data center. Blocks OWASP Top 10 attacks and uses more than 8,500 signatures for known vulnerabilities (CVEs), tuning itself so it doesn’t cut off normal requests; filters traffic from malicious IPs by F5’s reputation database, by country and by ASN; protects against request forgery (CSRF), masks card numbers and other sensitive data in the site’s responses, and checks GraphQL and JWT tokens. Filters network-layer (L3–4) and application-layer DDoS (L7 — machine learning spots abnormal spikes), limits request rates, and serves a JavaScript check or CAPTCHA. Built-in site scanning: finds everything the company exposes to the internet (servers, software versions, known CVEs) and runs automated penetration tests against the OWASP Top 10 for web apps and LLMs, with step-by-step evidence. Includes a CDN, secure DNS, load balancing and log export to a SIEM. The Enterprise package also detects malicious files in traffic, tracks visitor behavior and blocks malicious users, and protects against data theft through third-party scripts in the browser (Magecart). For APIs: it finds all APIs on its own — from traffic, in code and by crawling the site, including forgotten and “shadow” ones — allows only requests that match the OpenAPI schema, finds and masks more than 400 types of personal data in responses, and tests APIs for vulnerabilities before release. Advanced bot protection costs extra.
